lessons.title: Traffic paths and network explanations
lessons.prepare: Open the network-review chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Traffic paths and network explanations
body: Unit 1 · Week 14 · Lesson 1
Explain a path using addressing and device functions.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Explain a path using addressing and device functions. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which job belongs to a switch?
When does a client use its gateway?
slides.notes: A basic switch forwards local frames. The client ordinarily uses the gateway for off-subnet destinations under its mask. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Two library destinations
slides.notes: Use full addresses in the spoken explanation. A remote example such as 198.51.100.20 is fictional documentation data, not a live target. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A complete explanation
body: Need: retrieve a file from a remote network.
Address comparison: destination is not local.
Role: the gateway forwards towards that network.
slides.notes: Model the link between the requirement, mask comparison and routing action. A device name alone does not explain the outcome. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Local and remote traces
body: Trace one wired request to the local server.
Trace one wireless request to a remote service.
Compare the roles that differ.
slides.notes: The wireless trace adds the access point. The remote destination adds the gateway/routing role. Keep the physical drawing consistent with the explanation. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Write two traffic-path explanations.
State addresses, mask and relevant devices.
Have a partner identify an unsupported step.
slides.notes: Use need, device, action and outcome as a writing scaffold. Learners then revise independently. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: Two hosts are on the same stated subnet.
A: Basic local communication can use switching.
B: Every local frame must cross the Internet.
slides.notes: A. Do not confuse the presence of a router with a requirement to route every local exchange. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Explain why one destination is remote.
Name the routing action that follows.
slides.notes: Require the actual network comparison and gateway role. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: The library design workshop
lessons.prepare: Open the network-review chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: The library design workshop
body: Unit 1 · Week 14 · Lesson 2
Combine addressing, media and access decisions.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Combine addressing, media and access decisions. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which /24 addresses have special roles?
What must remain unique in an address plan?
slides.notes: For the ordinary practice /24, .0 is network and .255 broadcast. Host interface allocations must be distinct, including the gateway and server. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Library requirements
slides.notes: Use the chapter’s unchanged fictional brief. Do not invent a precise building distance or price. State assumptions where the scenario lacks facts. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A server allocation
body: Reserve 192.168.40.1 for the gateway.
Reserve 192.168.40.10 for the server.
Check proposed desktop addresses against both.
slides.notes: An allocation such as .40.20–31 gives twelve desktop addresses without reusing .1 or .10. Other coherent plans are acceptable. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A design critique
body: Check a partner’s wireless connection and gateway.
Trace a local and remote request.
Challenge one untested performance claim.
slides.notes: Require specific feedback about a link, address, access rule or evidence gap. Teacher checks the course diagram symbols. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Complete the library design and address table.
Explain two controls and a media choice.
Plan one test of a slowdown hypothesis.
slides.notes: Look for complete coverage of the brief. Allow alternate justified designs. This is ungraded practice with public explained answers. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A proposal gives fast equipment but no staff-file controls.
A: Speed alone meets every requirement.
B: The access requirement still needs evidence.
slides.notes: B. Performance and access protection are separate requirements. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Name one requirement your design supports.
Show the drawing, address or test that supports it.
slides.notes: Check concrete evidence against the brief rather than a general statement that the design works. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: Network scenario reasoning
lessons.prepare: Open the network-review chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Network scenario reasoning
body: Unit 1 · Week 14 · Lesson 3
Support each recommendation with a mechanism and limit.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Support each recommendation with a mechanism and limit. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: What evidence supports an access-control claim?
What does a ping reply establish?
slides.notes: Use a specific permitted/refused operation test. Ping establishes an ICMP response for that test, not web-service correctness. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: An explanation structure
slides.notes: Replace the old assessment slot with independent scenario practice. No mark allocation, submission condition or new graded task is introduced. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: An access recommendation
body: Need: students read resources without editing staff files.
Control: individual roles and narrow permissions.
Evidence: a read succeeds and an unauthorised write fails.
slides.notes: Explain where the rule operates. A firewall alone may not control a permitted application’s file operations. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Three short scenarios
body: Correct a gateway outside its client’s /24 subnet.
Explain an ICMP reply with a failed web service.
Investigate slower wireless transfers at busy times.
slides.notes: Expected: check intended local gateway; investigate service/name/access factors separately; gather radio and load evidence. Keep alternative explanations visible. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Answer two unfamiliar network scenarios.
Use need, mechanism, evidence and limit.
Compare with the explained answers and revise.
slides.notes: Support with a writing frame, then remove it for a fresh scenario. Accept equivalent technically coherent reasoning. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A download is slow and the cause is unknown.
A: Buy the fastest router immediately.
B: Gather evidence about the limiting link or service.
slides.notes: B. A diagnosis should justify the location and purpose of a change. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Write a recommendation for a fresh slowdown.
State one observation that could change your mind.
slides.notes: Look for a testable hypothesis and a genuine alternative rather than unsupported certainty. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: Network corrections and fresh transfer
lessons.prepare: Open the network-review chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Network corrections and fresh transfer
body: Unit 1 · Week 14 · Lesson 4
Use feedback to improve an explanation independently.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Use feedback to improve an explanation independently. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which network error have you corrected this week?
What evidence showed that it was wrong?
slides.notes: Let students choose an addressing, device-role, access or performance error. An exact correction is more useful than a confidence rating alone. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Common corrections
slides.notes: Use only errors present in learners’ work. Broadcasts consume resources within a broadcast domain, while routers ordinarily separate those domains. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A corrected explanation
body: Original: a new switch fixes all slow downloads.
Correction: locate the bottleneck first.
Transfer: what if only wireless users are affected?
slides.notes: The transfer suggests a wireless-specific investigation, while other evidence may still change the hypothesis. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Explain the correction
body: Show your original reasoning.
Name the exact mistaken rule.
Try changed data without the worked answer.
slides.notes: Partners explain the rule rather than copy corrected sentences. Example: change a destination network while keeping the sender mask fixed. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Complete a fresh address and traffic-path case.
Add an access-control test and a performance limit.
Choose one priority for consolidation.
slides.notes: Collect a short independent explanation for teacher planning. It remains an ungraded practice record. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: You copied the explained answer accurately.
A: That alone shows transfer to a new situation.
B: A changed example is needed to check understanding.
slides.notes: B. Accurate copying does not show that the underlying decision rule can be applied independently. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Explain one corrected rule from memory.
Write a changed example to revisit next week.
slides.notes: Check the new example exercises the same concept with different data or conditions. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF
